si_4_title: Revealing Individual Neuroanatomical Heterogeneity in Alzheimer Disease Using Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was used to predict regional cortical thickness, accounting for intersite variation and adaptively pooling parameter estimates across sites. The models were implemented using the PCNtoolkit (version 0.20).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: a neuroanatomical normative model indexed cortical thickness distributions using a separate healthy reference data set (n = 33,072), which used hierarchical Bayesian regression to predict cortical thickness per region using age and sex, while adjusting for site noise.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness measurements were obtained for 148 brain regions based on the Destrieux atlas, derived from T1-weighted MRI scans.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cortical thickness measurements across 148 brain regions were obtained from T1-weighted MRI scans... a neuroanatomical normative model indexed cortical thickness distributions ... to predict cortical thickness per region
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Verdi2023.pdf.md: Methods / Estimation of Cortical Thickness; Methods / Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as primary predictors, while site noise was adjusted for using a hierarchical framework that pools parameters across multiple scanning sites.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: used hierarchical Bayesian regression to predict cortical thickness per region using age and sex, while adjusting for site noise.
